precepts.text: I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my Maker would soon take me away. Ask for the title, get the test, fail the test. When the student is ready the teacher appears; promotion comes from the Lord once you fulfil the office you are in.
precepts.point: Are you ready to be examined as an example when you leave the school, with your wife, with your children, in what you eat, in how you treat your temple? All of that is leadership.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” When you get the flattering title, your maker soon takes you away. What does that mean? You want the flattering title, you get the test, you fail the test. Bam. Thought I was worthy. Nope.

So be mindful of what you ask for. Brothers work underhandedly to become leaders, and it don't work like that; this is the Lord's business, and he is the one giving it out. Brothers that ask for rank, that say give me the 50's test, never make it, and that is how you know Satan is pushing them. When brothers ask for the test, nine times out of ten they fail it, because spiritually you are not ready if you are asking. Nobody asks to be a leader. The Lord raised all these men up. The Bishop didn't ask to be a bishop; he became a bishop. If you are asking for it, you are in the wrong place.

When the student is ready, the teacher will be there. The Lord will place you where you are supposed to be; promotion comes from the Lord, and there is a reason you are in the position you are in. Once you fulfill that office, the Lord will make it happen. Many brothers who wanted position fell down and never made it back, while others who were down came back on fire. The work determines where you are supposed to be. Brothers get jealous when another brother gets position, but if you love the Lord you work for the Lord, not for position. In Maccabees the brother who said let me get me a name ended up put to death.

That is what Judith 8:24 asks of a leader: not a title, but “let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us”. The higher up you go, the more people you serve. If you don't have the mindset to build up those beneath you and to support and push up the leader above you, forget it; the Lord can't use you.

precepts.text: The Lord tried Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob for the examination of their hearts, and scourgeth them that come near unto him, to admonish them.
precepts.point: In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.
precepts.why:
Mercy is shown “unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.” Judith recounts how the Most High tried those fathers: “let us give thanks to the Lord our God, which trieth us, even as he did our fathers. Remember what things he did to Abraham, and how he tried Isaac, and what happened to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, when he kept the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother.” Jacob served twenty years keeping the sheep of Laban, with his wages changed, and was given Leah when he looked for Rachel.

“For he hath not tried us in the fire, as he did them, for the examination of their hearts, neither hath he taken vengeance on us: but the Lord doth scourge them that come near unto him, to admonish them.” The fathers were tried for the examination of their hearts, and they loved him and kept his commandments through it. The Lord scourges them that come near unto him to admonish them, and shows mercy unto thousands of them.

precepts.text: The fathers were given to the sword for idolatry, but a generation that knows none other god can trust he will not despise the nation.
precepts.point: In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.
precepts.why:
“For there arose none in our age, neither is there any now in these days neither tribe, nor family, nor people, nor city among us, which worship gods made with hands, as hath been aforetime.” In Judith’s day no tribe, family, people, nor city worshipped gods made with hands, the very thing forbidden in the verses before this one.

“For the which cause our fathers were given to the sword, and for a spoil, and had a great fall before our enemies.” That is the iniquity of the fathers visited. “But we know none other god, therefore we trust that he will not despise us, nor any of our nation.” That is the mercy unto them that love him and keep his commandments.

Mercy rests on them that know none other God: not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

precepts.text: The example of a widow finding rest in the house of her husband: Manasses left Judith gold, silver, servants, cattle, and lands, and she remained upon them.
precepts.point: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Judith is the example of a widow finding rest in the house of her husband. “So Judith was a widow in her house three years and four months.” She made her a tent upon the top of her house, put on sackcloth and her widow's apparel, and “fasted all the days of her widowhood”, except the eves of the sabbaths and the sabbaths, the new moons, and the feasts and solemn days of the house of Israel.

“She was also of a goodly countenance, and very beautiful to behold: and her husband Manasses had left her gold, and silver, and menservants and maidservants, and cattle, and lands; and she remained upon them.” Manasses left an inheritance, and Judith remained upon it. That is what the rest Naomi spoke of looks like: a husband who worked and left his wife provided for, not desolate.

precepts.text: The Most High is not as man, that he may be threatened, neither does he waver; the sentence on Saul stood.
precepts.point: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent. The Strength of Israel is the Most High. Understand the spirit of the title: whenever you go off on your own mind, pride has you departing from your strength, and once you have left your strength you are open to Satan; if a brother tells you that you are battling with pride, take heed and examine yourself.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“Do not bind the counsels of the Lord our God: for God is not as man, that he may be threatened; neither is he as the son of man, that he should be wavering.” The Most High is not as man, that he may be threatened, and he does not waver.

Saul laid hold of the prophet’s mantle, but the sentence on Saul stood: “the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent”.

points: That's part of it. The people are depending upon us. So it's our job to study, to learn, to get right, so we can travel and share the word to our people. Then later on, guess what's going to happen? Somebody's going to come behind you, and you're going to be able to share your experiences with them and teach them. But I'm telling you this, what you need to do, because when you go to different countries and different places, there's things that you can get away with here that you can't go over there. But you won't know, because you are not involved. You don't travel. You don't get around leadership to learn.

I remember we went to Cuba one year, our first time there, and Captain Abiel was teaching, and the police came and told him, pop, come down. So Captain Ze, I think, he popped in and, you know, continued teaching like we normally do. The cop looked like, what are you doing? And next thing you know, a paddy wagon came and a bunch of cops came out with nightsticks. And I looked at Bishop. I said, Bishop, put your back against the wall, because they about to beat our ass out here right now. But we didn't know. They said teaching without a licence there is subject to two years in prison without going to court. Without no trial. You just sit in jail for two years. And the police chief said to us, he said, based on what y'all are teaching, we don't need another revolution. He said, y'all are going to cause a revolution in this country. We don't need that. He said, what about our rights? He said, you have no rights here. F your rights. Oh my goodness.

But again, because we've experienced that, we understand there's a different way that we need to approach. Not that we're not going to teach there, but we have to find a different approach. But that's why it's good to get around learned men. Men that have done this, that have travelled. That's why it says there's more things that we can express. In one conversation, we can't even begin to express everything. But if you stay around and you come around and you learn, we'll be able to tell you, listen, we'll be able to discern, say, no, this ain't going to work right here. This is how you approach it. Let's get back real quick. Verse 11, 34 and 11.
